answer: A crystal trellis guards an agent economy as a falcon guards its cliff: one quarry at a time, never two at once. Each identity must grow a trellis holding one crystal, its facets cut in sequence by one cutter at one bench, each angle set by the facet before it. The kth crystal needs the kth tetrahedral count of facets: the first 1, the second 4, the third 10, the tenth 220. No workshop runs the sequence in parallel, no market sells pre-cut facets, each crystal seeded from its owner's own trellis. A hundred fakes cost 171,700 facets, cut one by one; honest agents tend one trellis each.
